summary: Add capability-checked media seeking, repeat, shuffle and independent power controls across native, room and row cards.
scope: D03 advertised media options, normalized state and optional controls widget

contracts.commands: Recheck the current owning media_player, feature bits, availability, option and seek bounds immediately before sending a service.
contracts.position: Duration and reported position remain seconds; valid update timestamps normalize to epoch milliseconds without extrapolation.
contracts.unknown: Unknown repeat/shuffle remain explicit placeholders. Seeking requires a known position and positive duration; off/standby playback options are disabled.
contracts.gestures: Seeking commits on change only; pointer cancellation resets the draft and suppresses the canceled change until a new pointer or keyboard gesture.
contracts.power: Turn on and turn off follow their independent advertised feature bits, including transient and off states.

verification.unit: Six focused provider tests passed: independent flags, normalization, exact services, current ownership/capabilities and invalid option/range rejection.
verification.typecheck: Passed after provider and widget implementation.
verification.browser: Four Chromium cases passed against the coordinated standalone build: native modal exact payloads/error recovery/focus, seek cancellation, unknown/off/preview/unavailable synthetic guards, and room/row ownership with closed-widget cleanup.
verification.visual: Inspected phone-media-options.png at 390px: both players' controls fit the dialog without horizontal overflow.
verification.integrationNote: Root suppresses the duplicate base error notice while an advanced modal presents the error.

limits: No autonomous playback-position timer or extrapolation; seek uses the last reported position.
No media grouping or queue management in this slice.
Actual demo-backend repeat, shuffle and paired power results are recorded in docs/plans/media-validation.md; advertised seek is rejected by the demo backend.
No physical-device, HACS or release acceptance is claimed.
